children: The Firmus IPO's failure to launch costs Maas Group a bull. Jefferies says the shelved IPO plan is a highly impactful event for Maas across both its earnings and equity investment in Firmus. It notes Firmus represents 50%-60% of Maas's revenues when the Construction Materials business is excluded. "In our view, risks have amplified," analyst John Campbell says. Most data centers that Firmus has in its pipeline don't have development approval. Jefferies notes Firmus still needs equity, and cuts its FY27-29 EPS forecasts by 5%-9%. "We acknowledge the situation is very fluid and a successful outcome on Firmus's private market raising endeavors could be a significant positive catalyst after the difficulties of the past week," Jefferies says, downgrading Maas to hold from buy. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
